question: What does the dimension of a vector space tell you?
direct_answer: It is the number of vectors in a basis.
expanded_answer:
Dimension measures how many independent directions are needed to describe the space. In \\(
\mathbb{R}^2\\) the dimension is 2, and in \\(
\mathbb{R}^3\\) it is 3. In ML, higher-dimensional spaces give models more axes along which data can vary, but they can also make learning and generalization harder.
key_points: Higher dimension means more representational axes
common_wrong_ideas: Dimension is the same as the number of data points
Dimension is the same as the magnitude of vectors
Every coordinate system gives a different dimension
